Civil Revision No. 9951(R) of 1991

Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, Advocate — For the Petitioner.

Government of Bangladesh representative by Deputy Registrar, Sylhet  ----- Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment:
3. The petitioner as defendant No. 4 contested the suit contending, inter alia, that the original owners left for India leaving the suit properties uncared for and they having become Indian nationals, the suit land became vested and non-resident property and vested in the Custodian of Vested Property and the plea of settlement to defendant No. 5, Alkas Ali is false and the pattas and rent receipts relied upon by the plaintiffs are forged and antedated and the plaintiffs acquired no title by virtue of purchase. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit holding that the settlement in favour of proforma-defendant No. 5, Sheikh Alkas Ali is false and the subsequent transfers to the plaintiffs had no validity. On appeal, being Title Appeal No. 82 of 1979 the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet dismissed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 27-2-1982 and 4-3-1982 respectively holding that the suit was not barred by limitation and the plaintiffs failed to prove their case so far as the alleged settlement by the original owners to the proforma-defendant No. 5 is concerned. 

 6. The opposite party Nos. 1-4 by filling counter affidavit denied the material allegations made in the application for review. It is further stated that the application for review is not maintainable and the grounds set forth in the petition are reproduction of the submissions made in the application and the same are not in conformity with the established principles of law. It is further stated that the review application is out of time by 890 days and admittedly an application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet was made by the opposite party on 27-1-86 and the petitioner had knowledge about the judgment and order passed in the Revisional application at least on 27-1-86 but the petitioner has not explained the said delay of one year nine months in filing this Review Application. So, the same is hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 8. Mr. SK Sinha, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, submits that the review application is hopelessly barred by limitation because there has been delay in filing the application by 890 days and no separate application under section 5 of the Limitation Act has been filed explaining the causes of delay for condonation of delay. In the application for review itself the period from 27-1-86 to 15-10-87 has not been explained and that period remains unexplained and the review application is therefore hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 9. Civil Revision No. 656 of 1982 was disposed of by the judgment dated 11-6-85 and the present review application under Order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed on 19-1-89. As per office report the application is out of time by 890 days. Admittedly no application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed for condonation of delay. In paragraph 8 of the review application it has been stated that after the judgment was delivered by this court in Civil Revision No. 656 of 1982 the opposite party through their lawyer filed an application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet on 27-1-86 for releasing the suit properties from the list of Vested Properties in view of the judgment passed in Civil Revision Case No. 656 of 1982 by this court on 11-6-85. It was further stated that thereafter on 15-10-87 the matter was sent to Fazlul Haque, Advocate for taking further step in the matter to protect the interest of the Government. Thereafter the learned Advocate sought for necessary fund for obtaining certified copies and on receipt of the necessary fund the learned Advocate applied for certified copies of the judgment of the courts below and obtained certified copy on 3-1-88 and thereafter the present revisional applicatidn has been filed. Thus from petitioner's own averment it is clear that the petitioner knew about the judgment passed in civil revision No. 656 of 1982 by this court on 27-1-86 when an application for releasing the suit property from the list of Vested Property was filed by the opposite party through their learned Advocate after the judgment was delivered by this court in Civil Revision No. 656 of 1982 on 11-6-85. The petitioner's case is that on 15-10-87 they sent the matter to Fazlul Haque, Advocate for taking further step and an explanation showing causes of delay from 15-10-87 to 3-1-88 has been offered but the period from that date of knowledge i.e. 27-1-86 to 15-10-87, when the matter was sent to Mr. Fazlul Haque, Advocate for taking further step in the matter to protect the interest of the Government remains unexplained. 

 11. The period of limitation for review of a judgment of this nature is 90 days from the date of decree on the order under Article 173 of the Limitation Act. This has been done with a view to securing finality of litigation. If this bar of time is not placed on the power of review it would mean that a judgment can never be final. Every order the effect of which is to vitiate the previous judgment is entirely foreign to the jurisdiction in review, especially when no time limit is placed on that power. 

 12. Mr. Sinha in support of his contention has placed the case of Fazal Din ETC. vs. Barkat Bibi, reported in PLD 1978 Lahore 1016 and submitted that in that case it was held that the scope of review is limited. It is further curtailed by law of limitation. Therefore, even if some new and important evidence had been discovered that would not entitle the party aggrieved to file a review petition according to his convenience and pleasure. The law of Limitation is to be strictly observed. He next cited the case of Rehabilitation Commissioner. Karachi vs. SA Majid, Liberty Cinema, Karachi, reported in PLD 1956 Cust WP 34 (Karachi) and submitted that in that case it was held that Articles 161, 162 and 173 of the Limitation Act prescribe periods for the review of judgment by the Court of Small Causes and the High Court. This has been done with a view to securing finality of litigation. If this bar of time is not placed on the power of review it would mean that a judgment can never become final. 

 14. Mr. Sinha, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, submits that such a long period is not supposed to be consumed in taking certified copies of the judgment of the court below and this explanation is not at all satisfactory. He further submits that there has been inordinate delay in filing the application for review and there would be no end of business of entertaining review application against the self-same judgment passed by the court if this review application is entertained. He further submits that in paragraph 8 of the review application itself the petitioner stated that they for the first time knew about the judgment dated 11-6-86 passed by this court in Civil Revision No. 656 of 1982 on 27-1-86 and the period from 27-1-86 to 15-10-87 i.e. about 1 year 8 months 18 days admittedly remains unexplained and on this ground alone the review petition is liable to be rejected. He further submits that there is no application under section 5 of the Limitation Act supported by an affidavit explaining the each day of delay in preferring this review petition. 

 15. It is true that an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act explaining the causes of delay in filing the review application should have been filed by the petitioner and that has not been done. The petitioner could explain the causes of delay in the petition of review itself but that has also not been done with respect to the period from 27-1-86 to 15-10-87 as we have already pointed out. I therefore cannot but hold that the review application is hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and in the light of my above discussion I hold that the review application being hopelessly barred by limitation is liable to fail.
